title: A cylinder rolls down a ramp

stimulus.title: A cylinder rolls down a ramp
stimulus.html: A uniform solid cylinder of mass M and radius R (I = ½MR², given) is released from rest at the top of a ramp of height H and rolls down without slipping. Air resistance and rolling friction are negligible. The system is the cylinder and Earth.

drawSpec.label: Energy bar charts for the cylinder-Earth system at the top and at the bottom of the ramp

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Draw energy bar charts for the cylinder-Earth system, one just after release at the top and one just before the cylinder reaches the bottom, with the gravitational potential energy Ug zero at the bottom. Use the columns Ug, Ktrans (translational kinetic energy) and Krot (rotational kinetic energy). Bar heights should show relative sizes.

rubric.point: Top: only U_g is nonzero (K_trans and K_rot are zero at release)
accept: a single U_g bar at the top

rubric.point: Bottom: U_g is zero and K_trans + K_rot equals the U_g bar at the top
accept: the two kinetic bars add to the original U_g
K_trans = ⅔ of the total, K_rot = ⅓
K_trans bar twice as tall as K_rot

parts.sample: Top: U_g = 3 units; K_trans = 0; K_rot = 0. Bottom: U_g = 0; K_trans = 2 units; K_rot = 1 unit. For a rolling solid cylinder, ½Iω² = ½(½MR²)(v/R)² = ¼Mv², half of ½Mv², so the translational bar is twice the rotational bar, and together they equal the original U_g.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the speed v of the cylinder’s center at the bottom of the ramp, in terms of H and physical constants, as appropriate. Begin your derivation by writing a fundamental physics principle or an equation from the reference information.

rubric.point: Starts from conservation of mechanical energy for the cylinder-Earth system with both kinetic terms: MgH = ½Mv² + ½Iω²
accept: U_g,top = K_trans + K_rot at the bottom

rubric.point: Uses rolling without slipping, ω = v/R, and I = ½MR²

parts.sample: Static friction acts at the contact point, which does not slide, so it does no work; mechanical energy of the cylinder-Earth system is conserved. MgH = ½Mv² + ½Iω². Rolling without slipping: ω = v/R, so ½(½MR²)(v/R)² = ¼Mv². MgH = ¾Mv², so v = √(4gH/3).

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: On the axes provided, sketch Ug, Ktrans and Krot of the system as functions of the distance the cylinder has traveled along the ramp, from the top (0) to the bottom (D). Label each line.

rubric.point: U_g is a straight line decreasing from its maximum to zero at D
accept: linear decrease of U_g with distance

rubric.point: K_trans and K_rot are straight lines starting at zero and increasing
accept: both kinetic energies linear in distance, from the origin

rubric.point: At every point K_trans is twice K_rot, and the three add to a constant (K_trans ends at ⅔ and K_rot at ⅓ of the starting U_g)
accept: K_trans line has twice the slope of K_rot

parts.sample: U_g falls in a straight line from MgH at 0 to zero at D, because the height drops in proportion to the distance along the ramp. K_trans and K_rot rise in straight lines from zero; K_trans ends at ⅔MgH and K_rot at ⅓MgH, so the K_trans line is always twice as high as the K_rot line, and U_g + K_trans + K_rot is constant at MgH.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: A hoop of the same mass and radius (I = MR², given) is released from the same height and also rolls without slipping. A student says it reaches the bottom with the same speed as the cylinder, because it has the same mass and falls the same height. Using your bar charts, your derivation and your graph, explain why the student is wrong and how the three representations agree with each other.

rubric.point: Bar charts: for the hoop the bottom bars K_trans and K_rot are equal (each half of U_g), so K_trans is a smaller share than the cylinder’s ⅔
Derivation: replacing ½MR² by MR² gives MgH = Mv², v = √(gH), smaller than √(4gH/3)
Graph: for the hoop the K_trans and K_rot lines coincide (equal slopes), while the cylinder’s K_trans line is steeper; all three representations show less translational energy, so a slower hoop
accept: same feature named in each representation and tied to a lower speed

parts.sample: The same mass and height give the same total energy MgH, but the hoop’s mass is all at its rim, so more of that energy goes into spinning. Bar charts: the hoop’s bottom chart has K_trans = K_rot = ½ of U_g, where the cylinder’s had K_trans = ⅔. Derivation: with I = MR², ½Iω² = ½Mv², so MgH = Mv² and v = √(gH), less than the cylinder’s √(4gH/3). Graph: the hoop’s K_trans and K_rot lines lie on top of each other, each ending at ½MgH, while the cylinder’s K_trans line is twice as steep as its K_rot line. All three show a smaller share of energy in moving along, so the hoop is slower at the bottom; mass cancels, shape does not.
